newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar prices weaken, stockists unload.
newsitem.headline: India sugar prices weaken, stockists unload.

text.p: Indian sugar prices weakened as new arrivals prompted stockists to unload on a market lacking consumer demand, traders said.
"Consumer demand remained negligible while fresh arrivals prompted fresh unloading by stockists," they said.
Earlier stockists had bought sugar on expectation of price rise but now amid sluggish demand they are liquidating holdings.
Mill owners remained active sellers despite lower than expected outstation buying. Higher offerings by the millers kept supplies plentiful in the Bombay market.

Prices for ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 10 rupees to 1,230/1,270 rupees per quintal while M-30 fell by 15/20 rupees to 1,265/1,350 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery also fell to 1,155/1,165 rupees from 1,170/1,195 rupees per quintal.

"Overall sentiment was subdued at the close, but some traders were expecting a recovery from the current level as government has so far not announced an earlier expected extra quota for the current month," one broker said.
Free sale quota for current month is 650,000 tonnes, compared to 800,000 tonnes last month.
